Subject: Recap + next steps from today’s RAG discovery call

Hi Jared —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap:
- Goal: vendor-facing knowledge base + troubleshooting assistant for Acme’s field engineers (short answers, grounded with policy snippets and service manuals).
- Data shape: ~120k docs (PDFs + HTML), 90% technical docs, 10% KB articles; sensitive PII filtered.
- SLOs: median latency < 350ms for short answers, 95th < 1s; Grounding requirement: >95% grounding on policy-critical queries.

Redwood recommendations (initial):
- Retrieval: dense embeddings + hybrid lexical filter for high-recall candidate set.
- Embedding model: use a 1k-d dense embedding (we’ll propose models in the next email).
- Reranker: start with our cross-encoder reranker tuned for grounding (higher precision@1, tolerates more compute per-query).
- Prompting: structured prompt with source attribution block + top-3 snippets.
- Metrics to track: Grounding Rate (source-linked answers), Hallucination Rate (manual eval), Precision@1 / MRR, and Coverage (recall) on legal/policy intents.

Requested next steps from your side:
1) Share a sample subset (100–200 docs) and a small eval set (20–30 user queries) that represent worst-case policy questions.
2) Confirm whether you can provide READ-only S3 access or export to a shared Drive link.
3) Any hard constraints on model choice (e.g., only open-source) or compute budget?

Deliverables from Redwood after we get sample data (ETA ~ 4 business days):
- RAG eval results CSV (baseline retrieval + 2 model variants).
- Prompt set v1 and recommended retrieval + reranker config.
- Short report with tradeoffs and recommended rollout plan (canary -> full).

I’ve attached a starter prompt set and checklist: [attachment: prompt_set_v1.txt (TXT, 6KB)].

If that timeline works I’ll kick off the evaluation with our SEs — Dylan and Priyom will be hands-on.

Best,

Hi Jared — quick technical notes answering your Qs and outlining the eval plan.

Reranker tradeoffs:
- Cross-encoder reranker (CE): computes pairwise relevance for query+snippet with a transformer (higher precision@1, significantly reduces hallucination when tuned for grounding). Downside: higher per-query latency and CPU/GPU cost (we run CE on GPU for speed). 
- Lightweight reranker (dense dot-product or bi-encoder re-ranker): much faster, lower cost, good recall but lower precision@1 and higher risk of selecting superficially similar but non-grounded snippets. Good for high-throughput, latency-sensitive apps; less safe for policy-critical answers.

Recommendation for Acme (given grounding >95% requirement):
- Phase 1 (eval): CE as primary reranker for the top-5 candidate set. Measure latency impact and precision@1. If tail latency or cost is unacceptable, we can hybridize: CE on top queries (policy-intents) + lighter re-ranker for non-critical intents.

Retrieval settings to evaluate (we’ll try three configs):
A) Dense-only (embedding recall top-100) -> retrieval scoring -> CE rerank top-10
B) Hybrid (lexical filter + dense embedding) top-200 -> CE rerank top-10
C) Conservative lexical-boost + dense top-100 -> lightweight rerank (dot-product) top-10

Embedding model recommendation (open-source):
- start with 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2' style embedding (efficient) for baseline recall; compare to a 1k-d dense model (higher fidelity) if recall gaps appear. We’ll provide concrete model names in the report depending on your infra constraints.

Grounding metrics (how we measure):
- Automated proxies: Source overlap score (token overlap between returned snippet and ground-truth doc), Attribution Confidence (model-assigned source weights). These are noisy but scalable.
- Human eval: binary grounded? for sampled queries (we recommend 200 eval queries for robust estimates but can start with 50 focused ones).
- Reported metrics: Grounding Rate (percent of answers with at least one correct source), Hallucination Rate (manual), Precision@1, MRR, and Latency (median + 95th).

Attachments: I ran the baseline quick-run on the sample subset you shared earlier and attached the result CSV and a short recommendations PDF. The CSV includes per-query retrieval candidates, reranker scores, and a grounding flag we computed heuristically.
[attachment: acme_rag_eval_results.csv (CSV, 28KB)]
[attachment: redwood_rag_recommendations.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

- Share a short runbook for canary config toggles (CE on/off, candidate set sizes).

If you’re available, I can walk product + infra through the tradeoffs in a 30-minute session next week.
